title: Direction, wrap, gap
learningObjectives: Explain direction, wrap, gap and build a practical layout with it.

understand.concept: flex-direction controls the direction of the main axis. flex-wrap determines whether items stay on one line or wrap onto multiple lines. gap sets spacing between flex items and lines without requiring margins on each item.
understand.whyItMatters: Wrapping helps layouts adapt to limited space. A nowrap row can overflow when items cannot shrink enough; a wrapped layout can form additional lines. Test long labels and translated text.
understand.analogy: A flex row can be like people standing in one line or forming additional rows when the room becomes crowded.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual flex layout follows the flex formatting algorithm and writing-mode rules.

explain.narrative: The chips wrap to new lines when the container is too narrow, and gap controls both row and column spacing.

examples.explanation: The chips wrap to new lines when the container is too narrow, and gap controls both row and column spacing.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered demonstration of the layout concept.

practise.guidedTask: Resize the preview and test flex-wrap:nowrap, wrap, and wrap-reverse. Keep all labels reachable.
practise.independentTask: Build a responsive component using this concept. Test long labels, narrow widths, and keyboard navigation.
hints: Inspect the flex container and items in developer tools.
Change one axis or alignment property at a time.
Test with translated or longer labels.
